comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth segment 2024 revenue breakdown and drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth revenues totaled $7.5 billion in 2024, a 7% increase largely driven by a 15% rise in non-interest revenue (including investment fees from Citigold, Wealth at Work, and Private Bank) and a 2% increase in net interest income due to higher deposit spreads and volumes, partially offset by higher mortgage funding costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citigroup report revenue growth in their wealth management segments driven primarily by higher asset management fees resulting from elevated market valuations. BAC explicitly attributes its 6% revenue increase in the Private Bank to 'higher asset management fees due to the impact of higher average equity market valuations.' Similarly, Citi’s Wealth segment reported a 7% revenue increase, where non-interest revenue (which includes investment fees) rose 15%, reflecting 'growth in client investment assets' at Citigold, Wealth at Work, and the Private Bank.
